summary: Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at Wellesley College, NYU (B.A.), Harvard (M.A.), and under Bernard Williams. She held positions at Harvard, Oxford, Brown, UNU-WIDER, and became Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Martin Baumann is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Leibniz University Hannover and his Habilitation at Leipzig University, becoming Professor of Religious Studies and seminar head at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Delhi, earned a doctoral degree at the University of Zurich, and served at the Ethnographic Museum at Zurich (1975) and the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

Martin Collcutt specializes in Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fitzwilliam College, the University of Cambridge, and Harvard (Ph.D.). He taught at Yokohama National University and the University of Tokyo before serving at Princeton University from 1975 to 2015.

Martin Delhey is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He has held positions at the University of Göttingen, the University of Hamburg, and Shandong University.

Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn, under mentors including Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Bonn, Heidelberg, Deccan College (1859–1866), and the University of Munich (1868).

Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (1915–1923, 1928–1958) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is a linguist and Indologist who completed his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Freiburg, studying under Eva Tichy and Helmut Rix. He served at the University of Freiburg (1999–2008) and became chairholder at Jena in 2013.

Martin King Whyte is a sociologist and sinologist educated at Cornell and Harvard (doctorate, 1971). His career includes faculty posts at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University (1994–2000), and Harvard University from 2000.

Martin Lehnert works in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Freiburg and was attested in 2016 as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich.

Martin Lowenthal is a scholar of Buddhist studies who trained under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen, Humboldt University, Heidelberg (Promotion), and Munich (Habilitation). He held posts at Munich, the University of Chicago (1990–2011), and the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (2013).
Martin Seeger is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Barend Jan Terwiel and held an attested post at the University of Hamburg in 2004.

Martin T. Adam specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and also studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Martin Willson was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His education included training under traditional teachers Lama Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Lambert Schmithausen and completed her doctoral degree at the University of Vienna (attested 2012), where she also held an academic post.

Martino Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2015) under the doctoral supervision of Donald S. Lopez Jr. and mentorship of Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954). He served on the faculty at the University of Michigan from circa 1949 to 1993.

Mary C. Wright was a sinologist and historian educated at Vassar College, Radcliffe College (PhD), and Harvard. She held positions at the Hoover Institution (1946–1959), Stanford University (from 1947), and Yale University (1959–1964 as associate, 1964 as full professor).

Mary Evelyn Tucker is a scholar of religion, sinology, and Japanology who earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University. She held professorships at Bucknell University (~1989–2006) and Yale University (~2006), and faculty posts at UC Berkeley and Harvard.
